deterministic_misspecification.interpretation: closed-world source+gauge elimination can be confidently wrong when the true input gauge is absent; independent held-out relation validation converts those observed wrong routes into abstentions in the matched deterministic screen.

noisy_validation_threshold_sweep.interpretation: under noisy relations, validation threshold creates a safety/coverage trade-off. At 5% noise, threshold 0.065 preserved wrong=0 in both matched and gauge-OOD samples while resolving about 89.6% of in-family commands. At 10% noise, threshold-only validation is not sufficient to guarantee wrong=0 on the in-family identification stage.

validation_rerank.interpretation: using validation to rerank all sources removes observed in-family wrong routing at 10% in this small screen, but a small gauge-OOD false accept remains. Open-world stochastic validation is therefore harder than ordinary noisy routing.

near_equivalence_analysis.interpretation: the remaining false accepts are not exact semantic equivalences in this search, but some wrong source+input-gauge hypotheses are extremely close on relation behavior. Random validation needs many queries to reliably expose a 0.5% disagreement region, especially on top of stochastic observation noise.

decision: safe open-world plugin admission needs an explicit model-misspecification/novelty test, not only posterior confidence inside a closed candidate/gauge family. Near-equivalent wrong hypotheses can require targeted disagreement queries or large validation budgets.
claim_boundaries: task noise modeled as iid relation-bit flips
threshold sweeps are small-sample screens, not calibrated production guarantees
gauge library is finite similarity transforms
